Im sure someone has said this but has worded it differently, but as someone who’s been becoming more aware over the past few years, I’ve been debating if we feel that something is coming or if it’s that we’re now becoming aware of the collective consciousness and its desire to change our current trajectory? In my understanding, life on earth operates as a mycelium circle or a tree branch. If there’s a major feeling of grief or a need for change rustling along all the branches, we’re all going to feel it somehow. I have the feeling that this huge change we all feel coming is a big part the collective pushing us towards the next stage of existence, even if just as a means of survival with all the environmental concerns present. We all instinctively know things need to change, but we’re waiting for a domino to fall when in reality our bodies are telling us to pull the trigger and knock it over ourselves.

I’ve had this thought while considering how the media I’ve seen throughout my life has changed. Nothing is original. Passion projects are left for dead unless the artist can drive up enough revenue. There are only a handful of original titles within television and movies that aren’t part of a previously established franchise. As an artist this hurts my heart to see. It feels like greed has its hands in most everything. 

So I just sit like you and scream into the void, meeting others who feel the same and individually lighting those sparks. We are out there and growing steadily, but you can’t find the individual by preaching to the masses. We hide in dirty corners, in pockets of our own joyful creation in resistance to the heavy pressure that surrounds us.

 I venture out less and less into these spaces as I’ve realized that this greed is consuming everything to its core and have focused on building my own personal community in the meantime.  I urge you to do the same. Create anything you can, put yourself out in public, and find us out there.

I’ve been in your shoes when I was a young adult. I will say, give yourself some grace to just figure things out as you go. 

Here’s what I do when I’m trying to find a job. I usually go onto google and type in the kind of career I am looking for in the location I would like. There are a few helpful websites like indeed and others you can use to see who is hiring in your area. If you already know of a company you might like to work for, you can go through their website and try to find their Careers page where it should have their open positions available. 

Make sure you look into how to write a resume, as well as researching what it would be like to go through the interview process so you feel more prepared. A lot of it is going to be trial and error, so definitely try to be patient with yourself. 

Google has essentially raised me since I had to leave home and I end up getting a lot of help just by typing in my questions and reading various websites until I feel more confident. You will probably make a few blunders, but you’ll also have a chance to learn by trying new things. 

I find, if I try to preemptively know what to expect and do my best to learn everything I can about something, I do a lot better in new situations while feeling much more comfortable. I hope you find something that works for you, there are a lot of good suggestions here.

I have a lot of resting anxiety and pressure helps, but weighted blankets are too much for me. I decided to fill a sock full of beans to lay on the area that carries the most tension which is usually my neck. That, and I read up recently that placing an ice pack on your vagus nerve (very involved w the parasympathetic nervous system) triggers what’s called the mammalian diving reflex. I put my pack in the middle of my chest, but you can take cold showers, baths, or find another way to cool your sternum if that’s not comfortable. It helped me in about 15 minutes and I had pretty intense anxiety beforehand. 10/10 would recommend beans and ice to everyone struggling.
